items.title: RTD steps up Op PEWA against foreign motorists without valid documents
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Road Transport Department (RTD) will intensify enforcement against foreigners driving or riding vehicles without valid driving documents, with vehicle owners who allow them to use their vehicles also facing action. RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the department would not compromise with foreign motorists found on the road without valid documents. He said he had instructed RTD senior enforcement director Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan to step up efforts to curb the problem.

items.title: Anwar defends moderate approach on Umno ties, says govt stability must come first
items.summary: KERALAM, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has chosen a moderate approach in handling differing views regarding the issue of cooperation with Umno within the Unity Government. Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan (PH) Chairman, stated that the government must remain stable because any overly harsh actions concerning the issue could result in losses for the country. Elaborating further, Anwar said various views were also voiced among political parties including PH, but such matters are normal within a coalition and should not be seen as something that could threaten government cooperation.

items.title: Anwar says Miti to pursue wider market access for Malaysian goods in India
items.summary: KERALAM, Sept 15 — The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) will follow up on efforts to widen access for Malaysian goods to the Indian market, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the matter was discussed during his meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, with several restrictions still needing to be addressed to facilitate trade between the two countries. He said the matter was also raised during his meeting with Keralam Chief Minister V.D.

items.title: Body in KLIA wheel bay: Cops appeal for family to identify unknown victim
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are seeking relatives or family members of missing persons who have been uncontactable since Aug 19 following the discovery of a man's body in an aircraft's wheel bay at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA). The appeal is focused on those who may have links to or were known to have been around KLIA since the date, as police work to identify the man whose body was found in the aircraft's wheel bay at Terminal 2 (KLIA2). KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner M Ravi said police had opened an investigation paper under the sudden death report (SDR) procedure on Aug 27 following the discovery of the unidentified body.

items.title: 'Food forest' grows community spirit at 1Razak Mansion
items.summary: The site, aptly named the 'Food Forest', has become more than just a place to grow fresh produce. For 64-year-old Alice Fernandez, the Food Forest is also a place to relax and connect with her neighbours. FROM FOOD FOREST 1.0 TO 2.0 Tang said the Food Forest at 1Razak Mansion represents Food Forest 1.0, a community-based model that combines food growing with participation by older residents, shared harvests, environmental stewardship, experiential learning and social regeneration.

items.title: Butterfield FB opens at 10pct discount despite strong IPO demand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Butterfield FB Bhd got off to a bitter start on its ACE Market debut today, opening at 43 sen, five sen or 10.42 per cent below its initial public offering (IPO) price of 48 sen. At 9.18am, Butterfield FB was trading at 44.5 sen, down 3.5 sen or 7.29 per cent, with 24.23 million shares changing hands. Butterfield FB raised RM72 million from the issuance of 150 million new shares.

items.title: Woman allegedly stabbed 13 times by husband after jealous row, suspect later surrenders
items.summary: Kulim police chief Supt Syamsul Sinring said the victim, identified as S. Sila, was taken to Kulim Hospital by family members and was pronounced dead at 9.30 pm. “The suspect also surrendered a folding knife believed to have been used in the incident,” he said in a statement yesterday. Syamsul said the suspect admitted to stabbing the victim 13 times using the folding knife.

items.title: Azalina: Let Negri Sembilan Umno resolve royal proclamation issue
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Negri Sembilan Umno and the state government should be given time and space to resolve an issue involving an alleged proclamation seeking the removal of state ruler Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the matter should be left to the state-level leadership to find a solution without interference from the federal government or Umno headquarters. Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim previously remained tight-lipped over the alleged proclamation seeking the removal of Tuanku Muhriz.

items.title: Anwar seeks closer Malaysia-Keralam ties in key sectors including digital economy, healthcare
items.summary: KERALAM, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for stronger cooperation between Malaysia and Keralam in key sectors, including the digital economy, healthcare, tourism and education. The Prime Minister said there was also potential to further expand tourism, business and people-to-people exchanges between Malaysia and Keralam. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, is accompanied on his working visit by Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.

items.title: Azalina: Ask Hannah Yeoh about Najib's deferred pardon application
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Any questions or explanations regarding the deferment of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon application should be directed to Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, said Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. The minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said she was not the minister responsible for the Pardons Board, while the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) under her ministry only served as its secretariat. "Any questions about what happened, why it was deferred and the new date should be directed to the minister responsible, Hannah Yeoh.

items.title: Anwar calls for stronger Malaysia-India synergy in E&E and semiconductor sectors
items.summary: KERALAM, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim called for Malaysia and India to strengthen synergy in the electrical and electronics (E&E) and semiconductor sectors to enhance their respective capabilities and benefit from each other’s strengths. He said Malaysia was positioning itself as a key player in the E&E and semiconductor sectors in Southeast Asia, while India also possessed considerable strength in these areas. I think it is important,” said Anwar.

items.title: Anwar, Muizzu to discuss trade, investment and tourism in Maldives meeting
items.summary: MALE, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will hold a meeting with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu today, the main event of his two-day official visit to the island republic. Anwar is scheduled to begin his official programme at the President’s Office at 9 am local time by attending the Official Welcoming Ceremony at Republic Square, before holding a one-on-one meeting with Muizzu. Anwar is scheduled to depart for Malaysia from Velana International Airport tomorrow afternoon, concluding his official visit to the Maldives.

items.title: Anwar arrives in Maldives for two-day official visit to strengthen bilateral ties
items.summary: MALE, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived in the Maldives tonight to begin a two-day official visit aimed at further strengthening Malaysia-Maldives bilateral ties, which dates back to 1968. The special aircraft carrying Anwar landed at Velana International Airport here at 8.12 pm local time (11.12 pm Malaysian time) with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu personally welcoming the Prime Minister. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, was accompanied by Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and a Malaysian delegation.

items.title: Anwar, Muizzu to discuss efforts to strengthen Malaysia-Maldives ties
items.summary: MALÉ: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will hold a meeting with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu today, the main event of his two-day official visit to the island republic. Anwar is scheduled to begin his official programme at the President's Office at 9am local time by attending the Official Welcoming Ceremony at Republic Square, before holding a one-on-one meeting with Muizzu. The Prime Minister is also scheduled to attend a press conference with the Malaysian media before attending an official luncheon hosted by Muizzu.

items.title: Air quality worsens across Malaysia: 38 stations in unhealthy bracket, Johor hardest hit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Air quality deteriorated to unhealthy levels at 38 monitoring locations across the country as of 8.45am today, according to Department of Environment (DOE) data, with Sarawak recording the worst reading in Malaysia. Banting, also in Selangor, registered 157. Selangor’s Kuala Selangor also featured, at 155.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher vs US dollar ahead of key central bank meetings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Tuesday, amid cautious sentiment ahead of key central bank meetings this week, an economist said. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the market focus is on the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting and Bank of Japan (BoJ) policy decisions. He said the three- and six-month US Treasury bills auction showed yields rose to 3.97 per cent and 4.06 per cent, respectively, up from the previous auction of 3.80 per cent and 3.89 per cent.

items.title: Three flee after Myvi crashes into motorcycle, killing Rela member
items.summary: Fazlizal Abdul Samad, 41, who was riding a Modenas Versys motorcycle, died at the scene following the 7.30am accident. District police chief superintendent Zaiham Mohd Kahar said police had launched a manhunt for the trio, who ran towards a nearby oil palm plantation after the accident. He said investigations revealed that the accident involved the suspects' Myvi, which was carrying two passengers, a Honda HR-V and the Modenas motorcycle.

items.title: Brazil's coffee exports jump in early September, government data shows
items.summary: SAO PAULO: Brazil's green coffee exports in September to the second week stood at a daily average of some 13,500 metric tons, up 51.5 per cent from the daily average in September 2025, government data showed on Monday. More details on Brazil's exports through the second week of September: Oil exports totaled 5.25 million tons, a daily average of some 656,200 tons, up 75.6 per cent yearly, after Brazil reported record output in June and July. Soybean shipments totaled 2.92 million tons, with a daily average of some 364,400 tons, up 9.2 per cent from a year earlier, following a record 2025/26 crop.

items.title: Three firms ordered to pay RM730,000 over negligence in Range Rover theft
items.summary: KLANG: A logistics company and two warehouse operators have been ordered to pay RM730,000 after a Range Rover was stolen from a warehouse in Port Klang. The Sessions Court here found Aktiv Worldwide Sdn Bhd, Advantage Warehouse Logistics Sdn Bhd and Westports CFS Sdn Bhd liable for negligence and breach of their duties in safeguarding the vehicle belonging to Fadzil Aziz Motor Sdn Bhd. The vehicle was shipped to Malaysia before being stored at Advantage Warehouse Logistics' premises in Westports, Pulau Indah, where warehouse operations were managed by Westports CFS.

items.title: PM: Decision to defer Najib’s pardon petition based on law, not personal prejudice
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The decision to defer former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s petition for a royal pardon was guided strictly by the Federal Constitution, the rule of law, and official legal advice, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. “A prime minister, whoever he is, must have a voice and give his views based on the law, on advice from the Attorney General and on the rules. Anwar said the question of Najib’s pardon must not be viewed through a personal lens, but evaluated against established legal benchmarks and good governance.

items.title: 37 areas record unhealthy API readings as haze persists
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Haze continued to affect several parts of the country today, with 37 air-quality monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 8am. Based on data from the Environment Department's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 30 monitoring stations recorded moderate API readings, while none were classified as having good air quality. Petaling Jaya, Batu Pahat and Indera Mahkota recorded 159 reading each.

items.title: Kulim husband stabs wife 13 times, jealousy believed to be motive
items.summary: District police chief Superintendent Syamsul Sinring said police had seized a folding knife believed to have been used in the attack. "The suspect admitted to stabbing the victim 13 times; seven times in the chest, five times in the stomach and once on the right side of her body, using a folding knife. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Plantation, healthcare, consumer product sectors attract RM263.7mil foreign inflows last week
items.summary: "Foreign institutions remained net sellers for the sixth consecutive week, recording RM160.3 million in net outflows, being net sellers on three out of five trading days during the week. In addition, local institutions ended a six-week consecutive net buying streak, recording RM127.4 million in net outflows. Meanwhile, retailers extended their net buying streak to three consecutive weeks, recording RM287.7 million in net inflows.

items.title: Wall Street ends down, calls for AI slowdown pummel chipmakers
items.summary: Shares of Nvidia declined 3.4 per cent, while Micron Technology dropped over five per cent. The PHLX chip index tumbled 5.9 per cent, reducing its 2026 gain to 57 per cent. The Nasdaq declined 0.56 per cent to 26,186.41 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.29 per cent to 52,421.17 points.

items.title: Ukraine ready for 'de-escalatory steps', says Zelenskyy
items.summary: KYIV: Ukraine president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday that the country was ready to de-escalate the war with Russia if its rival did the same, after US President Donald Trump announced that the foes had agreed to end strikes on energy targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!" Russia made no immediate comment.

items.title: Malaysians tighten purse strings on non-essentials
items.summary: Of the 16, five are staples companies, namely Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd, 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd, Life Water Bhd, QL Resources Bhd and Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd (F&N). Aw said revenue among consumer staples rose 8.6 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter (Q2) of 2026, while core net profit increased 11.1 per cent. Among the discretionary retailers, Eco-Shop's revenue grew 12.2 per cent year-on-year in Q2, while MyNews and 7-Eleven recorded increases of 12 per cent and 9.7 per cent, respectively.

items.title: Malaysian assets could be under pressure if Fed, BoJ tighten
items.summary: Market observers said risks are on a weaker ringgit, higher bond yields, foreign equity outflows and valuation pressure on rate-sensitive sectors, particularly real estate investment trusts (REITs), property and high-growth technology stocks. MBSB Research head of research Imran Yassin said simultaneous tightening by the US and Japan would create a less favourable liquidity environment as the Fed raises the cost of US dollar funding while higher Japanese rates increase the cost of yen borrowing. This could encourage some global investors to reduce leverage and exposure to Asian risk assets, including Malaysian equities.

items.title: MACC lodges police report against Muhyiddin's lawyer over alleged document disclosure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer has lodged a police report over the alleged disclosure of a classified document linked to former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's corruption trial involving the Jana Wibawa programme. According to the police report, an investigating officer informed the MACC officer that the document had allegedly been disclosed by Muhyiddin's lawyer, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, during proceedings at the Kuala Lumpur High Court yesterday. The report stated that at about 6pm, Amer Hamzah produced a document containing a copy of a recorded conversation involving Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad, who has been repeatedly mentioned during the trial.

items.title: 'I am the hoax buster': Trump rejects AI danger warnings
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Monday dismissed fears that artificial intelligence could wipe out humanity, repeatedly calling them a hoax and rejecting global calls to put guardrails around the fast-moving technology. Anthropic chief Dario Amodei, whose company makes the popular Claude AI system, opened the floodgates on Saturday when he called for AI companies to slow down. "AI should not exceed human control.

items.title: 2027 Budget tour must turn public feedback into policy, economists warn [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's nationwide tour for the 2027 Budget could mark a shift towards a more ground-up approach to fiscal policy, but economists say its success will hinge on whether feedback leads to concrete measures. Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Dr Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid said direct engagement with businesses, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and the public could move budget-making away from its traditionally top-down approach. Aimi said industry input could help the government identify potential problems with proposed measures before implementation.

items.title: Trump's son confirms Russian businessman paid for post-wedding festivities
items.summary: Donald Trump Jr. and Bettina Trump said in a jointly signed post on Bettina's Instagram account that their "dear friend" Umar Kremlev "very generously hosted two incredible nights" of festivities in the Bahamas in May. PUTIN TIES Russian President Vladimir Putin presented Kremlev with the "Order of Friendship" award in April 2026, according to an IBA press release, which featured a photo of Putin and Kremlev shaking hands. Bettina Trump's Instagram post was accompanied by 20 photos including one of the newlywed couple on a beach, and others of President Trump's other children Eric Trump, Ivanka Trump and Tiffany Trump.

items.title: ‘Our tebu is still sweet’: Tun Jugah’s son reflects on Sarawak, Malaysia at 63
items.summary: Singapore officially left Malaysia on August 9, 1965.) Linggi said Jugah played a key role in building support for the formation of Malaysia, bringing together 51 Iban headmen in Kapit on February 15, 1962, where they reached an agreement to support the formation of Malaysia. “My father worked very hard to make sure that Malaysia was a success,” he said.

items.title: Malaysia’s space ambitions start with changing public mindset, says Planetarium Negara director
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Malaysia’s ambitions in the space sector may begin not with rockets or satellites, but with something more fundamental: changing the way Malaysians see and understand space. Planetarium Negara director Mohd Zamri Shah Mastor said that before Malaysia can build a thriving space economy, it must first build something less tangible — a public that understands, accepts and is ready for it. School students explore the interactive exhibits at Planetarium Negara.

items.title: Contest attracts 25 students [WATCH]
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The inaugural New Straits Times (NST) "Heard The News Junior Journalists Challenge" yesterday attracted 25 students from SMK Seksyen 18, SMK Bukit Jelutong, SMK TTDI Jaya and SMK Seksyen 9 Shah Alam. The competition is an extension of NST's Heard The News initiative, a QR-code feature that allows readers to read along with audio clips of news articles in NST's printed and digital editions. An avid NST reader, she said the Heard The News audio feature presented news articles interactively to help younger people stay informed on current issues.

items.title: Aziz appointed deputy police chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid, who joined the force more than three decades ago, has been appointed deputy inspector-general of police. Special Branch director Datuk Seri Ibrahim Darus previously held the post in an acting capacity. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Aziz's appointment received the consent of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, on the advice of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the recommendation of the Police Force Commission, in accordance with Article 140 of the Federal Constitution.

items.title: Tan Chong lands Perodua EV deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tan Chong Motor Holdings Bhd has signed a three-year agreement with Perodua Sales Sdn Bhd to provide coating, painting and assembly line services for the national carmaker's battery electric vehicle (BEV) project in Serendah. Under the deal, Tan Chong's subsidiary, Tan Chong Motor Assemblies Sdn Bhd (TCMA), will provide electro-deposition coating, painting, assembly line rental, and related support. Perodua Sales will pay TCMA service fees and rental charges.

items.title: Mediators to hear Cambodia, Thailand maritime dispute
items.summary: PHNOM PENH: Cambodia and Thailand will face off before international mediators here this week in a long-standing dispute over valuable maritime resources, the latest spat between the feuding neighbours. Last week, Cambodia said it resorted to the conciliation process "after Thailand unilaterally terminated the agreed bilateral framework" through which the two nations had "negotiated their overlapping maritime claims for more than two decades". "The meeting marks another important milestone in the peaceful process initiated by Cambodia to resolve the countries' maritime differences," said Cambodia's Foreign Ministry.

items.title: Himalayas nearing tipping point as glacier melt threatens millions: Report
items.summary: HONG KONG: The Himalayas are approaching a tipping point as glaciers melt faster than a decade ago, threatening water security as the region approaches "peak water" by mid-century, according to a study released this month. As glaciers retreat, they are leaving behind unstable glacial lakes held back by little more than loose rock and ice, above valleys where millions of people live, the study found. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment.

items.title: Indonesia rescuers battle turbulent seas in search for 129 people after passenger ship capsizes
items.summary: JAKARTA: Hundreds of Indonesian rescuers including the coast guard and the navy raced on Monday to board a passenger ship that capsized in the Java Sea over the weekend as they searched for 129 people still missing, officials said, with the confirmed death toll at six. The Virgo Transport 8 ship carrying 243 people went missing in bad weather early on Sunday, the rescue agency said. Choppy waters with high waves and strong winds were impeding the search on Monday, said Mohammad Syafii, head of the national rescue agency.

items.title: UK PM cancels engagements after father's death
items.summary: LONDON: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has cancelled his upcoming engagements Monday and Tuesday due to the death of his father, his Downing Street office announced. Burnham has said in interviews that his father, Roy, had Alzheimer's disease and was living in a care home. He told podcaster Elizabeth Day that his father was unable to come and see him enter Downing Street along with his mother, but carers pointed out Burnham on television and thought he recognised him.-AFP © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Malaysia explores UAE interest in halal logistics, jobs and waste-to-energy
items.summary: KERALAM : Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim held discussions with UAE‑India Business Council, UAE Chapter (UIBC‑UC) leaders to explore cooperation in investment, logistics, employment and other sectors during his working visit here yesterday. Among those he met were Sharaf Group vice chairman Major General Sharafuddin Sharaf and EFS Facilities Services Group co‑founder and executive vice chairman Tariq Chauhan. Anwar said discussions with Sharafuddin included Sharaf Group's interest in leveraging Malaysia as a regional halal meat distribution hub, building on its cargo and logistics capabilities.

items.title: Croatian climber who scaled Mount Kinabalu illegally may face fine
items.summary: Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said Sabah Parks had lodged a police report over the incident involving the 46-year-old Mauro Persic, who is still in recovery. Last week, it was reported that a total of 43 search and rescue (SAR) personnel successfully brought Persic down after a five-day operation that also involved challenging terrain and rainy weather conditions. The rescue operation involved personnel from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM); the Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Malaysia (STORM) and Mountain Search and Rescue (MOCSAR) team, as well as mountain guides, porters, rangers and other security agencies.

items.title: Sabah mulls relocation of Kota Kinabalu central market
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — The Sabah government is mulling three new spots for the relocation of the Kota Kinabalu central market from the heart of the city. “The government will consider and decide which site is suitable for us to build the new Kota Kinabalu central market,” he told reporters after visiting the site. Hajiji said the proposed new market was envisaged as more than a conventional public market, with various activities and facilities incorporated into the development like both dry market and wet market, a cultural, local and tourism products centre, hawkers centre and fish wharf.

items.title: Sabah leaders call for apology from Umno man’s remarks on Christianity
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — Two Sabah leaders have called on Sepang Umno chief Datuk Noorazli Said to apologise over his controversial remarks concerning christianity and the Bible at the recent Umno general assembly. Tenom MP Datuk Arthur Kurup said Noorazli’s remarks were “highly inappropriate” and did not reflect the maturity expected of a political leader, while Tuaran MP and Tamparuli assemblyman Datuk Wilfred Madius Tangau described the joke as “grossly inappropriate and offensive”. Kurup, in a statement, said political differences did not give anyone the licence to make light of another person’s religion and beliefs for the sake of laughter or applause.

items.title: MACC officer denies key witness against Muhyiddin given ‘special treatment’, ‘immunity’ from own corruption case
items.summary: Under cross-examination by Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik, Mazery confirmed that Azman was a suspect in an MACC investigation in 2023 involving serious allegations of him and his associated companies KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and Addeen Engineering Sdn Bhd soliciting and accepting bribes. While confirming investigations showed Azman’s companies receiving RM9.35 million from Jana Wibawa contractors, Mazery disagreed that there is a “prima facie” case that Azman had solicited and received bribes. Mazery disagreed that his investigation on Azman is “biased”, and also denied protecting Azman.

items.title: Toy-ing with the bomb squad? Suspicious object in Sri Petaling destroyed, found to contain toy blocks (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — A suspicious plastic box found unattended in front of a shoplot in Bandar Baru Sri Petaling earlier today contained toy building blocks after a police bomb disposal unit was called to the scene. Kuala Lumpur police chief Commissioner Datuk Fadil Marsus said authorities were alerted to the box at about 12.57pm after a 33-year-old woman reported the discovery. “Initial checks found that the object had a high radiation reading, which prompted the deployment of a Bomb Disposal Unit, together with the Bukit Aman Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear and Explosive (CBRNE) Unit, to the scene for further checks and evaluation,” he said.

items.title: Haze update: 22 areas register unhealthy air quality at 4pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — A total of 22 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 4pm today. According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, four areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Serian (181), Sri Aman (166), Samarahan (153) and Kuching (152). Forty-five areas had a moderate API reading while only Kangar in Perlis had a good API reading.

items.title: Ex-director faces 71 cheating charges over RM4.7m used car scam
items.summary: He was accused of cheating Wong Yoong Jed, a director of Viso Capital Sdn Bhd and Lio Capital Sdn Bhd, by deceiving him into believing that various vehicles had been purchased. This induced Wong to transfer RM1.69 million from Lio Capital and Viso Capital into Buycar2u’s bank account. Before Judges Norma and Muhammad Ilmami, the accused faced 30 charges involving RM1.98 million and 15 charges involving RM1.02 million, respectively.

items.title: Transport minister: Private vehicle ownership transfer inspection fees will remain standardised, no price competition
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH, Sept 14 — The multi-operator system for motor vehicle inspection services does not allow licensed operators to compete on price, but requires them to focus on the efficiency and quality of their services, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke. He said the fee for private vehicle ownership transfer inspections (M.V.15) will remain standardised and regulated by the government through the Road Transport Department (JPJ) at all licensed centres. On operational efficiency, Loke said the inspection process at licensed private centres takes less than 20 minutes when conducted according to the prescribed schedule, adding that the results are transmitted directly to the JPJ system, facilitating the vehicle ownership transfer process.

items.title: Carried by teenager porter, rescued Croatian climber says Kinabalu ordeal broke his heart
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — Croatian climber Mauro Persic has expressed regret over the risks he took after being found injured and alone on Mount Kinabalu for eight days, but said the ordeal strengthened his faith in human compassion. Persic, 46, said the rescue operation was a humbling experience, particularly when rescuers and porters had to carry him down because he was too weak and injured to continue on his own, Berita Harian reported. 40 people risking their lives to save one.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: Second multi-purpose mission ship under construction in Turkiye to be completed by end‑2027
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The second Multi-Purpose Mission Ship (MPMS), which is currently under construction in Turkiye, is expected to be completed and handed over to the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) by the end of next year, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the first MPMS vessel was expected to arrive in March next year, a month before the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA). Saifuddin Nasution said he would travel to Istanbul, Turkiye, at the end of this month to personally inspect the progress of the vessel’s construction.

items.title: Anthony Loke calls for Pakatan Presidential Council meeting to discuss recent political developments after Umno assembly
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH, Sept 14 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he will propose to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim that the Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council convene to discuss recent political developments following statements made at the Umno General Assembly. He said the recent statements raised concerns regarding political certainty and stability, which could affect investor and public confidence in the country. The Prime Minister must also make this clear with all component parties,” the Transport Minister said.

items.title: Penang Port Commission, PPSB to offer free ferry services on Malaysia Day
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — The Penang Port Commission (SPPP) and Penang Port Sdn Bhd (PPSB) are offering free ferry services to Malaysians on September 16 in conjunction with Malaysia Day celebrations and the Keretapi Sarong Festival. SPPP chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the offer applies to trips from both ferry terminals, Pangkalan Sultan Abdul Halim (PSAH) in Seberang Perai and Pangkalan Raja Tun Uda (PRTU) here, in accordance with the existing service schedule. According to him, during last year’s Malaysia Day celebration, a total of 10,094 pedestrians and 1,909 two-wheeled vehicles utilised the ferry service for round trips.

items.title: Chief of Defence Force: MAF proposes reinstating multi‑agency border‑security framework used under former national task force
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) has submitted a proposal to the National Security Council (NSC) to reinstate a multi-agency operational framework modelled on the National Task Force (NTF) to bolster national border security. Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the proposal, submitted through the National Operational Management Committee, would bring together various agencies including the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA), the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM), and the Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM). He said the strategic coordination of enforcement agencies has proven more effective in addressing security vulnerabilities along the country’s land and maritime borders.

items.title: Two‑year‑old mauled by stray dogs in Batu Pahat to undergo reconstructive surgery
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Sept 14 — A two-year-old girl mauled by stray dogs outside her grandmother’s home in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, is expected to undergo reconstructive surgery soon as she continues to fight for her life. Nur Haira Wafiqah Mohammad Hamizi was critically injured in the Sept 6 attack by five dogs, suffering severe head and facial wounds. Previously, the authorities caught seven dogs, including five puppies, which attacked Haira.

items.title: Free entry to three Penang heritage sites for two days starting tomorrow in conjunction with Malaysia Day
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — Three heritage sites in Penang will offer free entry for two days from tomorrow in conjunction with the fifth anniversary of Penang Hill’s recognition as a Unesco Biosphere Reserve and Malaysia Day. State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the three sites are the Penang State Automotive Gallery, Fort Cornwallis and the Penang State Museum. “The public and tourists from Malaysia and abroad, are welcome to take this opportunity to explore history, appreciate the state’s heritage, gain a deeper understanding of Penang’s past and discover Malaysia’s rich and diverse cultural heritage,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Federal Court hears PKR’s argument that Zuraida’s RM10m bond was reasonable; decision reserved
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The Federal Court was told today that the High Court’s decision ordering former Ampang MP Datuk Zuraida Kamaruddin to pay RM10 million to Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) for breaching a bond with the party was reasonable. “Zuraida admitted that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million, while the operative clause fixed RM10 million as the sum payable upon the occurrence of the stipulated events,” he said during PKR’s appeal against a Court of Appeal decision reducing the bond payment from RM10 million to RM100,000. “The recital recorded Zuraida’s admission that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million.

items.title: New Lawas Hospital expected to evolve into specialist centre to cut long‑distance referrals, says deputy health minister
items.summary: LAWAS, Sept 14 — The new 76-bed Lawas Hospital is expected to evolve into a specialist hospital, thereby reducing the local population’s reliance on distant hospitals. “I hope that God willing, medical specialists will be permanently based at Lawas Hospital, rather than relying on scheduled visiting specialists. I hope this facility will become a specialist hospital,” she said at the Lawas Hospital project handover ceremony here today.

items.title: Abdul Aziz appointed Deputy Inspector‑General of Police
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Management Director Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid has been appointed Deputy Inspector-General of Police, effective September 9. He joined the PDRM on July 1, 1995, and has served in various departments throughout his career, including the Management Department, Special Branch, Criminal Investigation Department, Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department, Commercial Crime Investigation Department, Logistics and Technology Department, and Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department. Abdul Aziz has held several key positions, including Management Director, Deputy Director of Special Branch, Deputy Director of Narcotics, Penang Police Deputy Chief, Principal Assistant Director of Management Policy/Human Resource, and Principal Assistant Director of the Special Integrated Investigation Team.

items.title: Sixteen drownings in Pahang this year, Bomba urges public to respect warning signs
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 14 — A total of 16 drowning deaths have been recorded in Pahang so far this year, and the public is urged to prioritise safety when engaging in activities near rivers, waterfalls, and beaches. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations and rescue, Mohd Salahuddin Isa, said key safety measures include heeding warning signs and refraining from swimming in areas identified as dangerous. “To date, 16 drowning cases resulting in 16 deaths have been recorded across the state; we advise the public to always prioritise safety and understand the risks associated with recreational areas.
